title: Mine Lamp Checker
premise: A long drama of a mine-lamp checker at the lamp room and shaft mouth. Xiaomei and Xiaotan are easily confused; the methane alarm goes intact-alarming→sensor-failed→calibrated-repaired; the mine rubber-tired vehicle crashes down the shaft and must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_on_duty: Mine-lamp checker Han Lei around forty, orange helmet, deep-blue miner's clothes, methane alarm on the chest, rough hands.
states.weary_injured: The same Han Lei: helmet brim cracked, left arm bandaged, miner's clothes thick with coal mud, still forcing his steps.
states.left_post: Han Lei has left his post; only his old miner's clothes and orange helmet remain in the lamp room—he himself no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Apprentice Xiaomei of fifteen or sixteen, yellow helmet, orange fluorescent armband, slight build but stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Xiaomei in his early twenties, still in yellow helmet and orange fluorescent armband, tall and steady.

states.intact_alarming: A palm-sized methane alarm, yellow case red light, mine crest on the side, readout clear.
states.sensor_failed: The same methane alarm with water-failed sensor, red light flashing wild, screen garbled.
states.calibrated_repaired: After calibration and probe replacement the methane alarm alarms steadily again, maintenance sticker on the case.

states.intact: An oilcloth-cover inspection log packed with roadway numbers and gas readings.
states.coal_dust_stained: The same inspection log muddied by coal slurry and water stains, writing blurred into black clumps.

states.intact: A dark-green mine rubber-tired vehicle, white 'Lamp-Check-03' sprayed on the nose, spare mine lamps in the rear bed.
states.shaft_wrecked: After falling into the incline shaft, the mine rubber-tired vehicle has a twisted frame and wheels off—a wreck that can no longer drive.

states.young_rival: Young Xiaotan close in build to Xiaomei, same yellow helmet but blue armband, coal scar on the chin, defiant look.
states.disguised: Disguised Xiaotan still wears a blue armband, coal scar deeper, expression darker.

segments.action: At dusk, Han Lei pushes open the iron door into the lamp-room workshop and first checks the methane alarm on the bench.
A row of five self-rescuers hangs on iron hooks in the lamp room; Han Lei tightens each valve in turn.
Two airdoor bells hang above the airdoor; Han Lei reaches out and lets them ring softly for inspection.
Han Lei circles the workbench, checking whether mine-lamp charging docks are overheating.
Through the iron window Han Lei watches the dimming sky light at the shaft-mouth shed.
The methane alarm's red light flashes steady; Han Lei records the baseline reading.
Han Lei sits on a wooden stool in the lamp-room corner and dozes.
Han Lei opens the inspection log and records that day's gas peaks for each roadway.
Han Lei draws a gas curve in the inspection log.
Han Lei closes the inspection log and returns it to the workbench iron box.
The methane alarm beeps softly; Han Lei nods in confirmation.
Han Lei wipes coal ash from the log cover with a rag.
In the morning shaft-mouth shed, Han Lei greets young Xiaomei driving the mine rubber-tired vehicle in.
Xiaomei jumps down from the rubber-tired vehicle and hangs the key on a shed post.
Han Lei points to three spare mine lamps on the workshop iron rack, teaching Xiaomei to read the full-charge green tags.
Xiaomei crouches by the shaft-mouth shed, studying the cage iron gate with curiosity.
Han Lei explains underground escape routes; Xiaomei nods seriously.
Xiaomei looks back at the parked dark-green rubber-tired vehicle, eyes tense and excited.
Han Lei has Xiaomei first try on a self-rescuer facepiece on the surface.
In the dim materials-store corridor, Xiaotan in a blue armband looks up from behind a pile of pit props.

segments.action: In rainy season, Han Lei dries damp mine-lamp batteries one by one in the lamp room.
Han Lei brushes carbon from the charging docks with a bristle brush.
At dawn, Han Lei checks the shift roster in the shaft-mouth shed.
Han Lei hangs a raincoat on a shed post and listens to the cage cable creak.
In midsummer, Han Lei turns on the lamp-room exhaust fan to clear the carbide smell.
Han Lei zeros the methane alarm and records ambient temperature.
When autumn wind rises, Han Lei checks whether airdoor seal strips have aged.
Han Lei trial-writes new roadway codes on a blank page of the inspection log.
On a frosty night, Han Lei lights an emergency lamp and checks flashlight batteries.
Han Lei wraps the rubber-tired vehicle battery in a cotton blanket against overnight freeze.
On a heavy-snow day, Han Lei sweeps thin snow from the shaft-mouth shed stone steps.
Han Lei breathes on his hands and tightens self-rescuer valves.
At spring's start, Han Lei clears weeds from the abandoned air-shaft mouth.
Han Lei runs airtight tests on all five self-rescuers one by one.
Han Lei posts a new escape-route map on the lamp-room wall corner.
Around Dragon Boat Festival, Han Lei fumigates the materials store with sulfur smoke against damp and insects.
Han Lei resticks the green tags on the spare mine lamps.
Han Lei paces alone in the shaft-mouth shed, silently reciting escape callsigns.
After rain stops, Han Lei opens the lamp-room window and hears eave water drip into an iron bucket.
Han Lei replaces a worn helmet pad with a new one.
Another dusk, Han Lei sits by the alarm listening to the fan's low hum.
At night Han Lei rises and turns the lamp-room heater up one notch.
Han Lei wipes and trial-fits newly arrived lamp-head glass.
At the abandoned air-shaft mouth Han Lei wipes the No Entry sign.
Han Lei checks the rubber-tired vehicle chassis for cracks.
Han Lei marks hazard points on the roadway diagram.
Han Lei wrings out a coal-stained rag and hangs it under the rear eave.
On a full-moon night, Han Lei looks at the shaft mouth from the window; the iron door gleams cold.
Han Lei sorts the lamp rack so heads hang down to dry.
On the inspection-log flyleaf Han Lei writes the new season's lamp-check notes.
Han Lei polishes both airdoor bells bright.
Hearing forklift noise from the materials store, Han Lei keeps logging readings.
Han Lei glues a cracked toolbox shut.
In the lamp-room corner Han Lei stacks old lamp heads awaiting repair.
Han Lei shuts the iron door tight against night cold wind into the lamp room.
Another Qingming, Han Lei sets a bunch of wildflowers at the air-shaft mouth.
Han Lei rolls roadway drawings into a tube and binds them with a rubber band.
Han Lei tests the alarm buzz; the sound is clear and sharp.
Han Lei sits silent in the lamp room, listening to the fan moan a long while.
Han Lei cuts worn orange-armband cloth into rag stock.
At dawn, Han Lei patrols the shaft-mouth shed; the dark-green rubber-tired vehicle sits under the shed.
Han Lei crouches to check tire pressure on the rubber-tired vehicle.
Han Lei walks to the workshop rack; those three spare mine lamps still show green tags side by side.
A yellow explosion-proof battery cart passes the shaft mouth—broad flat body, not the lamp-check rubber-tired vehicle.
Han Lei stands in the shaft-mouth shed, logging airdoor open-close counts.
Han Lei hangs a wet raincoat on the shaft-mouth shed wooden rack.
Han Lei pats coal ash from his sleeve and looks back at the lamp-room light.
After Grain Rain, Han Lei teaches new workers airdoor signals in the shaft-mouth shed.
Han Lei refolds sun-dried raincoats into the iron cabinet.
In summer heat, Han Lei lays a wet cloth on the alarm case to cool it.
Han Lei checks the rubber-tired vehicle rear bed and moves damp lamp heads to the upper layer.
On an autumn night, Han Lei mends loose inspection-log pages under an emergency lamp.
Han Lei rotates all five self-rescuers out for inspection.
At first snow, Han Lei sweeps a narrow path at the lamp-room threshold.
Han Lei fully recharges the spare mine lamps.
Hearing copper bells ring softly, Han Lei keeps correcting the shift handover record.
Han Lei pushes open the shaft-mouth shed door so a draft clears the damp.
At the air-shaft mouth Han Lei hangs a rain tarp.
Han Lei puts a scorched fuse into an iron box.
At night Han Lei dreams of gas over-limit, wakes, and writes it in the log.
Han Lei rinses the lamp rack with clean water.
Han Lei wipes the escape map clean and renails it to the north wall.
Han Lei pulls weeds from shaft-mouth stone seams.
Han Lei hangs the self-rescuers back on iron hooks; number tags have faded some.
Before lights-out Han Lei takes one last look at the alarm's green light.
Han Lei wipes clean a yellow helmet an apprentice left in the lamp room and sets it aside.
Hearing the materials-store lock for closing, Han Lei rises and locks up.
By a charcoal fire Han Lei dries his gloves.
Han Lei shifts the airdoor bells aside to show the just-repaired airdoor.
Han Lei hangs dust-sampling filter membranes on a shed post to dry.
On the log's last page Han Lei draws a gas-depth comparison.
Han Lei silently recites tomorrow's roadway numbers and steps out of the air-shaft mouth.
Han Lei pushes the rubber-tired vehicle to the wall foot, clearing repair floor space.
Hearing a distant whistle, Han Lei blows out the emergency lamp.
Another rainy night, Han Lei alone keeps watch by the alarm until dawn.
Han Lei packs newly issued dust masks into paper bags.
On a stormy night the incline shaft floods; lamp-room alarms blare suddenly.
In the shaking, methane-alarm readings jump wildly.
After a piercing buzz, the methane alarm sensor fails from water; the red light flashes wild.

segments.action: To the shaft mouth comes support worker Lao Wei, orange helmet muddied, build close to Han Lei's.
Then safety inspector Lao Zhou arrives too, white helmet and camouflage coveralls, talking beside Han Lei.
Lao Zhou points at the yellow explosion-proof battery cart, asking if it belongs to the lamp-check team.
The inspector leaves; Han Lei alone remains in the shaft-mouth shed.
Lao Wei shoulders pit props and bows farewell.
From the materials store comes girl Xiaoxia in a light-brown hard hat; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Xiaomei.
Xiaoxia practices counting rock bolts; Han Lei shakes his head—she is not Xiaomei after all.
Xiaoxia shyly lowers her head and sets her hard hat straight.
Years later at dusk, Han Lei with a bandaged left arm stands at the abandoned air-shaft mouth.
